decisions.decision: Session continuity via PROJECT_STATE.json + SESSION_LOG.md + ARCHITECTURE.md in docs/
decisions.rationale: AI agent reads PROJECT_STATE.json on session start to resume; SESSION_LOG.md provides narrative context; ARCHITECTURE.md is living design doc

decisions.decision: Code optimized for AI maintainability, not human readability
decisions.rationale: Per project objective: AI is sole developer and maintainer

decisions.decision: Plugin architecture modeled after IDE extensibility
decisions.rationale: End users customize via AI-driven IDE; framework must have clean extension points

decisions.decision: Client/server with REST HTTP/HTTPS; RDBMS for persistence
decisions.rationale: Per project requirements; well-understood patterns with broad language support

decisions.decision: ISA-95/IEC 62264 alignment for data model and operations categories
decisions.rationale: All major commercial MES systems align with ISA-95; ensures industry-standard interoperability

decisions.decision: Event-driven architecture with internal event bus
decisions.rationale: Dispatching, plugin hooks, and equipment integration all depend on event-driven patterns

decisions.decision: Start with single-site discrete manufacturing; process/batch as future plugin
decisions.rationale: Widest initial audience; ISA-88 batch support deferred to backlog

decisions.decision: 25 modules identified and registered with IDs for project tracking
decisions.rationale: Enables referencing functionality by ID; documented in MES_SURVEY.md Section 4

decisions.decision: Python 3.12+ / FastAPI / SQLAlchemy 2.0 / PostgreSQL for server stack
decisions.rationale: Python is #1 AI-friendly language; FastAPI has best REST/async/OpenAPI support; SQLAlchemy is best Python ORM; PostgreSQL is industrial-grade RDBMS

decisions.decision: React + TypeScript for GUI clients (Runtime GUI and Design-Time)
decisions.rationale: Widest AI training corpus for frontend; large component ecosystem; shared codebase between two GUI clients

decisions.decision: Uniform module internal structure: models.py, schemas.py, service.py, routes.py, events.py, exceptions.py
decisions.rationale: AI predictability — agent always knows where to find/add code; eliminates searching

decisions.decision: Plugin framework with manifest.yaml, MESPlugin base class, 7 extension point types
decisions.rationale: Clean contracts, declarative metadata, type-safe extension points for AI-driven customization

decisions.decision: In-process async event bus with dot-notation topics; future Redis/NATS swap for distributed
decisions.rationale: Simple for single-server; same interface scales to distributed; plugins subscribe declaratively

decisions.decision: JWT authentication with RBAC authorization; 4 default roles (admin, engineer, operator, viewer)
decisions.rationale: Industry standard; stateless; fine-grained permissions via dot-notation strings

decisions.decision: Implementation order: Layer 0 (foundation) → Layer 1 (physical/product) → Layer 2 (production) → Layer 3 (execution) → Layer 4 (quality/analysis)
decisions.rationale: Each layer depends on the previous; ensures incremental buildability and testability

decisions.decision: UUIDs for all primary keys; soft deletes via is_active flag; cursor-based pagination
decisions.rationale: UUIDs avoid sequence conflicts in distributed/plugin scenarios; soft deletes preserve audit trail; cursor pagination scales better than offset

decisions.decision: Multi-RDBMS support: PostgreSQL (default), SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite (dev). End user selects via connection string.
decisions.rationale: Many manufacturing environments run SQL Server or Oracle due to enterprise licensing; SQLAlchemy dialect system makes this near-zero-cost; portability rules enforce ORM-only queries

decisions.decision: OIDC SSO for authentication; MES never stores passwords; supports any OIDC-compliant IdP (Entra ID, Keycloak, WSO2, Okta, etc.); local auth as dev/fallback only
decisions.rationale: Factory MES should delegate auth to enterprise IdP; OIDC is the industry standard; JIT user provisioning and IdP group-to-role mapping eliminate manual user management

decisions.decision: ERP adapters as vendor-specific plugins behind abstract interface; 5 ERP vendors supported: SAP S/4HANA, SAP ECC, Oracle Cloud/EBS, Microsoft D365 F&O, Infor M3; transform layer isolates ERP field mappings from core
decisions.rationale: Each factory has a different ERP; abstract interface + transform layer means swapping ERP is a plugin change; vendor APIs researched to ensure realistic interface design

decisions.decision: Equipment communication via OPC-UA (asyncua), MQTT (aiomqtt), Modbus TCP (pymodbus), HTTP/REST (httpx), ZeroMQ (pyzmq); MOM integration via Kafka (aiokafka), RabbitMQ (aio-pika), JMS brokers via STOMP (stomp.py) or AMQP 1.0 (proton/Qpid); distributed event bus supports Kafka, NATS, Redis Streams
decisions.rationale: OPC-UA is the primary industrial standard; MQTT covers IoT/edge; MOM integration needed for factories with existing message infrastructure (JMS, Kafka, RabbitMQ); all Python libraries are async-capable and actively maintained

decisions.decision: Alembic-based migration strategy: sequential numbered migrations, module ID in filenames, data-safe patterns (expand-contract for breaking changes), separate plugin migration chains with table prefixes, mandatory downgrade(), CI validates full upgrade/downgrade cycle, production runbook with backup-first policy
decisions.rationale: Production MES databases contain irreplaceable manufacturing data; migrations must be safe, reversible, testable, and predictable for AI agents; plugin schema isolation prevents coupling plugin lifecycle to core releases

decisions.decision: DT-CLIENT: React+TS design-time configuration environment for plant model, product defs, routes, materials, quality setup, auth admin, plugin management, import/export. Uses TanStack Query, React Hook Form + Zod, Headless UI + Tailwind, OIDC auth. Shared @mes/ui component library between DT-CLIENT and RT-CLIENT. Config health dashboard with completeness warnings. Aggregate API endpoints for tree views.
decisions.rationale: Reference implementation proves API sufficiency for full configuration; shared component library avoids duplication between DT and RT clients; tree/aggregate endpoints reduce round-trips; Zod mirrors Pydantic for consistent validation; end users can replace DT-CLIENT entirely via AI-generated alternatives

decisions.decision: TEST-CLIENT: Python Textual TUI with 5 tabs (API Explorer, Mock ERP Simulator, Equipment Simulator, Event Monitor, Scenario Runner). Auto-discovers endpoints from OpenAPI spec. Mock ERP receiver (FastAPI) catches outbound reports. OPC-UA server simulator (asyncua) and MQTT publisher simulate equipment. YAML-based scenario engine for end-to-end test flows. Data seeder creates sample factory via API.
decisions.rationale: No real factory or ERP during development; test client proves full system works end-to-end; Python TUI can import server Pydantic schemas directly, run OPC-UA/MQTT simulators, and run mock HTTP server — all impossible in a browser client; terminal-based works over SSH, in containers, and CI

decisions.decision: ISA-95 route ownership boundary: ERP owns route creation, versioning, and cost-rate assignments (Level 4). MES holds a local execution copy of routes synced via ERPInboundAdapter.sync_routings(). MES uses routes for execution sequencing, data collection anchoring, outbound cost-posting mapping, and runtime deviation (rework/skip/alternate). MES never creates routes for new products — DT-CLIENT route editor exists only for standalone/demo mode.
decisions.rationale: Clear ISA-95 Level 3/4 boundary prevents scope creep into ERP territory (cost rollup, capacity planning, standard costing) while documenting why the MES must still store route/operation data locally for real-time execution

decisions.decision: Equipment state machine: pluggable architecture via equipment_state_model extension point. Three plugins: PackML (ISA-TR88, 17 states), SEMI E10/E58 (6 states + sub-states), OEE/TPM (6 states). Only one active at a time. All plugins map states to 4 canonical DispatchCategory values (available, busy, unavailable_planned, unavailable_unplanned) and 5 OEEBucket values. DISPATCH engine queries only canonical categories — never raw plugin states. EquipmentStateLog denormalizes dispatch_category and oee_bucket at write time for fast queries.
decisions.rationale: Different industries prefer different state models (packaging→PackML, semiconductor→SEMI E10, general→OEE/TPM). Plugin approach avoids forcing a single standard while guaranteeing dispatch correctness via canonical category invariant: WIP only dispatched to equipment where dispatch_category=AVAILABLE

decisions.decision: Use pydantic-settings for configuration management
decisions.rationale: Standardizes environment variable loading and validation for the FastAPI application

decisions.decision: Route definition models (ProcessRoute, RouteStep, StepParameter) live in PROD-DEF module per §5.2/§6.3 grouping; core/routing/ reserved for ROUTE-ENGINE (Layer 2 runtime execution)
decisions.rationale: Routes are tightly coupled to ProductDefinition (FK, nested endpoints); separating them would create unnecessary cross-module imports. ROUTE-ENGINE is distinct — it handles runtime next-step logic, rework loops, and alternate route selection

decisions.decision: BOMItem references materials via material_code (string) not FK; FK to material_definitions deferred to MAT-MGMT implementation (Layer 3)
decisions.rationale: MAT-MGMT module does not exist yet; adding a FK now would create a circular dependency. String reference allows BOM items to be created and tested independently

decisions.decision: UOM uses affine conversion model (base_value = value * multiplier + offset) — handles temperature and all linear unit conversions. Custom/packaging units (can, case, pallet) use the same model with user-defined types.
decisions.rationale: Single formula covers SI, imperial, and packaging units without a separate conversion-pair table. Each uom_type has a base unit (multiplier=1, offset=0); all other units in the type store their factor relative to the base.

decisions.decision: DT-CLIENT bootstrapped early (during P3) to build editors alongside server modules. React+TS+Vite+Tailwind+TanStack Query+React Hook Form+Zod+Headless UI. Vite dev server proxies /api to FastAPI at :8000.
decisions.rationale: Building the editor immediately after the server module validates the API design and gives a visual tool for testing. One editor per server module, added incrementally.

decisions.decision: Architecture §3.3 added: Multi-Language Client Integration — OpenAPI SDK generation for C#/Java/C++, JWT auth from non-browser clients, WebSocket event streaming for all languages.
decisions.rationale: REST API is inherently language-agnostic; documenting SDK generation and authentication patterns ensures equipment controllers (C/C++/C#) and ERP bridges (Java/C#) can integrate without guesswork.

decisions.decision: OPC-UA equipment adapter: asyncua as optional dependency (pip install mes-ai[opcua]). Supports None/Sign/SignAndEncrypt security, anonymous/username/certificate auth, tag-based NodeId resolution with caching, data change subscriptions, address space browsing, configurable state tag with dispatch/OEE mapping.
decisions.rationale: OPC-UA is the primary industrial communication standard per D020. Optional dependency keeps the core footprint small. State mapping to dispatch categories ensures integration with DISPATCH engine.

decisions.decision: MQTT equipment adapter: aiomqtt as optional dependency (pip install mes-ai[mqtt]). Topic-based tag mapping under configurable prefix. Local value cache from retained messages and wildcard subscription. TLS with optional client certificate auth. Username/password broker auth. Event-driven subscriptions (no polling). JSON/numeric/boolean payload auto-decoding. Configurable state topic with dispatch/OEE mapping.
decisions.rationale: MQTT is the primary IoT/edge protocol per D020. Pub/sub nature requires a local cache for read_tag (returns latest received value). Wildcard subscription for tag discovery replaces OPC-UA browse. Same state mapping pattern as OPC-UA for dispatch engine integration.

decisions.decision: Oracle Cloud ERP adapter: httpx-based REST client (no OData, no CSRF). Oracle Fusion REST APIs with offset/limit pagination, Oracle IDCS/OCI IAM OAuth2 token flow with optional scope. Organization-code-based filtering (not plant-code like SAP). Oracle field naming (WorkOrderNumber, ItemNumber, OrganizationCode) mapped to MES canonical DTOs. 60 unit tests covering transforms, config, client headers, inbound/outbound adapters, and factory integration.
decisions.rationale: Oracle Cloud ERP is a major enterprise ERP per D019. REST APIs (not OData) with different pagination and field naming conventions than SAP. Same 4-file vendor package pattern (config, client, transform, adapter) ensures consistency across ERP adapters.

decisions.decision: Plugin system redesign: two directories (plugins/system for contributors, plugins/user for end users), DB-driven install lifecycle (available→installed→enabled→disabled→uninstalled), manifest parameters (ManifestParameter: name, type, description, required, default, secret), enhanced metadata (comment, category, origin, author). Parameter values provided at install time, validated before enabling. REST API: install/uninstall/enable/disable/config endpoints. CLI: offline list/search/info + server-backed install/uninstall/enable/disable. DT-CLIENT: Available/Installed tabs, parameter input form on install/detail pages.
decisions.rationale: Original plugin system auto-loaded all plugins with no install/uninstall lifecycle, no parameter declaration, and no system/user distinction. Redesign enables end users to add custom plugins to a separate directory, configure parameters at install time, and manage lifecycle through UI or CLI without modifying plugin code.

decisions.decision: Unified adapter-plugin architecture: AdapterFactory and BaseAdapter removed. Every adapter is now a plugin (manifest.yaml + plugin.py in plugins/system/). PluginManager exclusively manages adapter lifecycle (discovery, install, enable, start, stop). 3 new extension point types added (erp_inbound, erp_outbound, test_equipment). Adapter interfaces remain as standalone ABCs in adapters/ with connect/disconnect/health_check methods. Plugin wrappers use composition: plugin wraps adapter class, handles lifecycle, delegates operations. Config env vars for adapter selection removed; adapter choice is now plugin install/enable. Catalog endpoint dynamically generated from discovered adapter plugins. CLI adapter subcommands removed.
decisions.rationale: Two separate lifecycle management systems (AdapterFactory vs PluginManager) created duplication, configuration confusion (env vars vs manifest parameters), and split the extension model. Unifying means one lifecycle (plugin lifecycle), one config mechanism (manifest parameters + DB), one management interface (plugin REST API / CLI / DT-CLIENT UI), and one discovery mechanism (manifest.yaml scanning). Vendor adapter implementation code stays in adapters/ as importable libraries — only the lifecycle wrapper moves to plugins/system/.

decisions.decision: SAP ERP Simulator plugin: realistic mock SAP S/4HANA environment in plugins/system/sap_erp_simulator/ (5 source files). SAPDataCatalog provides 20 materials, 3 products with BOMs/routings, 5 production orders, 4 work centers — all with realistic SAP field names and numbering conventions. SAPTransformLayer handles bidirectional SAP↔MES DTO conversion. SAPSimulatorOutbound generates SAP-style document numbers per type (confirmation=49x, goods movement=50x, scrap=53x, labor=CAT-, downtime=PM-, quality=QM-). 55 unit tests.
decisions.rationale: No real SAP system available during development. Realistic simulator enables end-to-end testing of the full ERP integration path (inbound sync + outbound reporting + confirmation tracking) without SAP connectivity. Same data catalog shared by inbound and outbound ensures consistency.

decisions.decision: ERP Simulator GUI: standalone React+Vite client at clients/erp_simulator/ (port 5174, separate from DT-CLIENT on 5173). Dashboard with adapter health check, 6 inbound sync pages (orders, materials, products, BOMs, routings, work centers), 6 outbound report pages (completion, consumption, scrap, labor, downtime, quality), confirmations viewer. 13 new REST API endpoints added to server/src/mes/adapters/erp/routes.py.
decisions.rationale: GUI provides visual interface for manually triggering and inspecting ERP integration operations. Separate app avoids coupling with DT-CLIENT. New REST endpoints expose adapter operations (sync/report) that were previously only available programmatically via plugin manager.

decisions.decision: MATERIAL_TYPES expanded from 3 to 7: raw, intermediate, finished, semi, consumable, packaging, spare. SAP type mapping: ROH→raw, HALB→semi, FERT→finished, VERP→packaging, HIBE→consumable, ERSA→spare, UNBW→intermediate.
decisions.rationale: Original 3 types insufficient for SAP material type diversity. Manufacturing needs distinct categories for packaging, consumables, and spare parts to support material management and costing.

decisions.decision: Shared ERP-agnostic UOM normalization utility at adapters/erp/uom_mapping.py. Maps uppercase ERP codes (KG, G, M, L, EA, PC, etc.) to MES UOM symbols (kg, g, m, L, EA, PC). Case-insensitive lookup with pass-through for unknown codes. Applied to all UOM fields in SAP and Oracle transforms (materials, production orders, BOM items).
decisions.rationale: SAP uses uppercase UOM codes (KG, M) but MES DB stores lowercase (kg, m) per units_of_measure FK constraint. Different ERPs may use different casing. Shared utility avoids per-ERP UOM mapping duplication and ensures all transforms produce DB-compatible UOM values.

decisions.decision: ERP Simulator GUI material CRUD now persists to database. Sync endpoint upserts (create/update/reactivate). Create/update/delete endpoints call MaterialService. Delete is soft-delete via MaterialService.delete_material().
decisions.rationale: Simulator materials only existed in memory. Sync, create, update, and delete must persist to DB so materials appear in DT-CLIENT and other modules that query material_definitions table.

decisions.decision: ERP route sync persists to MES database via upsert (match on product_id+name+version for routes, route_id+sequence for steps). ERP owns route creation; MES holds execution copy with work_cell_id and parameters.
decisions.rationale: ISA-95 Level 3/4 boundary: ERP defines WHAT operations; MES adds WHERE (work_cell_id) and HOW (parameters, cycle times). Sync endpoint converts ProcessRouteDTO list to MES ProcessRoute+RouteStep rows.

decisions.decision: RouteStep.erp_operation_number (String(50), nullable) maps MES steps back to ERP operations for outbound reporting. Populated automatically during sync from ERP.
decisions.rationale: ERP outbound completion reports require the ERP operation number to post against the correct cost center/routing step. This field bridges MES execution steps to ERP costing operations.

decisions.decision: WIP completion events (wip.lot.completed, wip.unit.completed) auto-enqueue ERP outbound completion reports via event bus handlers. No manual reporting needed.
decisions.rationale: Event-driven approach ensures every production completion is reported to ERP without operator intervention. Handlers look up ProductionOrder.erp_reference and RouteStep.erp_operation_number to build the completion report, then enqueue to the outbound retry queue.

decisions.decision: Step Transitions: StepTransition model (from_step_id, to_step_id, condition, is_default, priority, label) enables graph-based routing with rework loops, MRB branches, and disposition-driven paths. Conditions: always, on_pass, on_fail, on_rework, disposition. Evaluation priority: disposition > result > always > default. Linear sequence fallback when no transitions defined. REST CRUD under /steps/{id}/transitions.
decisions.rationale: Linear-only routing cannot model rework loops, MRB disposition, or conditional branching. Graph-based transitions with condition evaluation and linear fallback preserve backward compatibility while enabling real manufacturing process flows.

decisions.decision: CPG Demo: Server-side seed module with two POST endpoints (/demo/seed-cpg-erp, /demo/seed-cpg-plant) that orchestrate all service calls. One-click buttons in ERP Simulator and DT-CLIENT call these endpoints.
decisions.rationale: Server-side orchestration avoids 30+ sequential client-side API calls and ensures transactional consistency. Demonstrates ISA-95 structure with realistic juice bottling line: 7 route steps, rework/MRB branches, 6 work cells, 7 equipment, dual fillers for dispatch.

decisions.decision: Electronics Demo: Discrete-manufacturing PCB assembly demo with unit serial number tracking. Same seed pattern as CPG (two POST endpoints, one-click buttons). Product type 'discrete' with serial template SN-{order}-{seq:05d}. 8 route steps including AOI branch to rework loop and MRB disposition. Dual PNP placement machines for dispatch.
decisions.rationale: Complements CPG (process/lot-tracked) with a discrete/unit-tracked scenario. Demonstrates serial number auto-generation, AOI-driven pass/fail/rework branching, and MRB disposition paths. ECB- prefix avoids data collisions with CPG-.

decisions.decision: ISA-95 Part 4 Process Segment: route steps carry equipment_class_id (nullable FK → EquipmentClass) to declare what class of equipment is needed. Dispatch resolves equipment from class membership at runtime.
decisions.rationale: ISA-95 process segments define equipment requirements by class, not by specific equipment. This decouples route definition from physical equipment layout and enables dispatch flexibility.

decisions.decision: StepEquipmentRequirement model: explicit per-step equipment declarations with use_type (required/preferred/alternate) for fine-grained dispatch control. Unique on (step_id, equipment_id).
decisions.rationale: ISA-95 allows process segments to declare specific equipment requirements alongside equipment class requirements. The use_type field enables dispatch strategies to prefer certain equipment while allowing alternates.

decisions.decision: StepMaterialRequirement model: per-step BOM with material_use (consumed/produced), quantity, UOM, position. Separate from product-level BOM for step-level material granularity.
decisions.rationale: ISA-95 process segments define material requirements at the operation level. Step-level BOM enables material consumption tracking per route step rather than only at the product level.

decisions.decision: Dispatch 3-tier equipment resolution priority: (1) StepEquipmentRequirement rows → (2) equipment_class_id membership → (3) legacy work_cell_id. Empty options if no constraint defined.
decisions.rationale: Provides backward compatibility with existing work_cell_id-based routing while enabling ISA-95 process segment equipment resolution. Explicit requirements take priority over class-based, which takes priority over legacy.

resumeInstructions: On session start, read this file first, then SESSION_LOG.md for narrative context. Check 'currentPhase' and 'currentTask' to know exactly where to resume. Reference module IDs from 'modules.registry' when discussing functionality.
